transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (OceanPay, Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (OceanPay, CTO), Lina Gomez (OceanPay, Infra)
Links shared: deck: https://tinyurl.com/redwood-optimize-oceanpay, benchmark sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmarks, security pack: https://redwood.ai/security-pack

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize module focusing on batching and prefix/KV cache options, with a simple cost model and recommended pilot steps. Transcript below (auto-generated, medium quality):

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through Optimize today, focusing on batching and caching recs for your payment flows. Marcus and I will go through the cost model, and then we'll leave time for q's. sound good?
[00:35] Aisha: yep, sounds good, thanks. quick context: our main use case is fraud scoring and chat-assist for merchant support, mix of short and long prompts, 60% short (<= 64 tokens) 40% longer. throughput spikes during settlement windows.
[01:10] Marcus: cool, thanks Aisha. first thing: batching — there are two levers we recommend: dynamic batching at the runtime level and request-level batching in the API. dynamic batching will group concurrent requests to improve GPU utilization; you tune max_batch_size and max_latency_ms to hit your latency SLO.
[01:45] Tom: can you give a concrete number? like what max_batch_size should we use for gpus we run?
[02:05] Marcus: typical for a 80GB GA100 style instance we'd see good throughput with max_batch ~16-32 for medium models, but it really depends on the model and sequence length. in our cost model i put assump of 20 avg batch size for your traffic shape.
[02:40] Lina: so batching will obviously increase latency tail right? we care about 95th pct under 120ms
[03:05] Sofia: right, so tradeoff: with dynamic batching you set a max latency budget — e.g., 50ms queuing + 70ms model time = ~120ms total. if queuing grows beyond that the runtime will flush. we also support prioritized routing for e.g. interactive vs background.
[03:45] Marcus: moving on to caching: two flavors we recommend — prefix caching (simple, works at token prefix level) vs KV-cache (more explicit key-value cache of KV states for long-running conversations). prefix is lower complexity, KV-cache gives more hit-rate for long convos.
[04:20] Aisha: what's the difference in implementation effort?
[04:35] Marcus: prefix caching is basically automatic at the stream level: we hash prefixes and serve common prefixes from cache; KV-cache requires you to persist and rehydrate KV states — requires API changes to pass cache keys but gives higher reuse for stateful RLHF-style convos.
[05:00] Tom: what about memory overhead?
[05:15] Marcus: KV-cache stores KV blobs which increases memory per conversation — we suggest TTLs and eviction policies. in our numbers we assumed 4KB per active convo on avg, but depends. prefix cache is more memory-friendly but lower hit rate for varied prompts.
[05:50] Sofia: now the cost model slide — high level: we compared three configs: hosted baseline (no cache, small batch), batching only, batching + prefix cache, batching + KV-cache. with a 60% prefix hit rate we project ~30% token cost reduction; with 60% KV hit rate we project up to ~50-55% reduction.
[06:30] Aisha: hmm 50% is big. how sensitive is that to hit rate?
[06:45] Marcus: very — small changes in hit rate produce linear changes in token savings. we ran a sensitivity chart in the sheet: at 30% hit rate KV gives ~20% savings; at 70% it's ~60%. the batch size also compounds savings because fewer in-flight tokens overall.
[07:20] Tom: can you share the math quickly?
[07:30] Marcus: sure — simplified: total token cost = tokens_generated * cost_per_token; tokens_generated is a function of prefix miss rate. if prefix hit rate h then saved tokens = h * average_prefix_length. add batching that amortizes per-request overhead so per-token cost reduces. exact formulas in the sheet.
[08:05] Sofia: pulled up the benchmark slide — here's a sample run we did for a payments dataset: baseline 100 tps, p95 latency 85ms, unit cost $0.012/token (example). with batching+kv we hit effective cost $0.0065/token and p95 110ms (still within some SLOs).
[08:40] Lina: those p95s look close to our 120ms threshold, ok. how about failure modes if cache rehydration fails?
[09:00] Marcus: on a cache miss we simply fall back to full generation; we have circuit-breakers and fallback policies — we also keep per-route metrics so you can alert when miss rates spike.
[09:30] Aisha: regarding privacy/compliance: do KV blobs ever leave our VPC?
[09:45] Sofia: good Q — for Private deployments KV blobs can be stored in customer-managed storage, and we support KMS/HSM integration. for Dedicated you can opt for encryption-at-rest and network restrictions; we'll share the SOC2 and network diagrams.
[10:10] Tom: Lina, do you have specific questions on our infra side?
[10:20] Lina: yes, want to confirm TLS mutual auth, SSO integration, and whether the cache endpoint is behind our firewall. also curious about autoscaling impact on cache coherence.
[10:40] Marcus: mTLS supported, SAML SSO supported for console; for cache coherence our routing and control plane ensure consistent eviction policies — but across autoscaled nodes you may see warming periods; we recommend a warmup strategy with you initial pilot.
[11:15] Sofia: let's walk the pilot plan — short pilot: 2-week run, mirrored traffic (~100k requests/day), run A/B: control is baseline, variant is batching+kv with TTL 24h, we collect cost delta and quality metrics (perplexity or your custom eval).
[11:45] Aisha: does Redwood help set up the mirror?
[11:55] Marcus: yes we'll provide a small proxy config and scripts; we can also run a synthetic generator if you prefer.
[12:15] Tom: about deployment mode: are you recommending Dedicated or Private for us?
[12:30] Sofia: it depends — for heavy throughput and controls Dedicated is common; for strict data residency and KMS controls Private (VPC/on-prem) is better. given you require strong compliance and we need KMS integration for KV blobs, Private might be appropriate but Dedicated with customer-managed encryption is a possible compromise.
[13:05] Lina: cost delta between Dedicated and Private?
[13:20] Marcus: Private has a platform fee and infra overhead; we can give a comparative estimate in the pricing sheet — i'll include a sample TCO for your traffic shape.
[13:45] Aisha: any latency difference between Dedicated and Private?
[13:55] Marcus: if Private is on-prem you avoid inter-region hops, might gain latency; Dedicated in our managed cluster is similar but network path depends on region — we'll test during pilot.
[14:20] Tom: got it. some random Q: what's the impact of quantization on batching and KV-cache?
[14:35] Marcus: quantization reduces per-token compute and memory which increases effective batch capacity; KV-cache interacts well with quantized paths but rehydration must be converted correctly — we have tested 4-bit quantized models with KV rehydrate in our runtime. small caveats around numerical fidelity — we monitor regen quality in the evals.
[15:10] Sofia: ok jumping back to the cost model sheet: i flagged two rows specific to OceanPay assumptions (avg conv length, prefix length, tps spikes). Marcus, can you call out the sample numbers?
[15:30] Marcus: sure — assumptions: avg tokens per request 180, avg prefix 40, 25% long-run convos with repeated prefixes, 60% short prompts. we modelled 3 hit-rate scenarios: 30/50/70% and batch sizes 8/20/32. savings vary accordingly — all in the sheet.
[16:05] Aisha: did you account for extra memory in pricing?
[16:15] Marcus: yes memory overhead for KV is included as a small per-hour infra delta; we also show amortized cost per active convo.
[16:40] Tom: if we wanted to run benchmarks, what artifact do you need from us?
[16:50] Marcus: sample traffic trace (anonymized), expected SLOs, and a small set of prompts for quality evals (10-20 labeled examples). Lina to share network topology and egress constraints.
[17:15] Lina: i'll share by friday. question — how disruptive is integrating the cache keys into our app stack?
[17:30] Marcus: minimal — we provide SDK snippets; for KV you surface a cache_key and store/lookup flow. prefix caching is zero-touch for many customers.
[17:55] Aisha: can we do a small POC first with prefix cache only to measure hit rates?
[18:10] Sofia: absolutely, that's low friction and a good first signal.
[18:30] Tom: any notable competitor differences here? what do OpenAI/Anthropic do?
[18:45] Marcus: OpenAI provides caching at the application layer typically; some vendors have built-in prefix caching but KV-cache with runtime rehydrate is more specialized. Anthropic sometimes emphasizes safety/eval features. we'll include a short competitor note in the deck.
[19:05] Aisha: ok, security stuff: can you send SOC2 + network diagrams?
[19:15] Sofia: yes will attach in follow-up.
[19:30] Marcus: quick demo time — i'm going to show the Console Optimize tab and the batching slider, then flip to the cost-model worksheet.
[19:45] [screen share noises] Marcus: here you see the route config, batching settings, and cache toggles. you can set max_batch, batching window ms, and cache policy (ttl, eviction).
[20:20] Aisha: i see a field 'cache warmup' what's that?
[20:30] Marcus: warmup preloads expected keys into the cache so you avoid cold misses during a traffic spike. useful for settlement windows.
[20:50] Tom: can we upload a list of known prefixes into warmup?
[21:00] Marcus: yes, we accept a CSV of top prefixes or provide an API to populate.
[21:20] Lina: re: metrics, what do we get out of the box?
[21:30] Marcus: token-level cost, per-route hit/miss rate, kv-store size, avg rehydrate time, and per-model p95/p99. we push traces to your honeycomb/Datadog if you want.
[21:55] Aisha: nice. question around coherency: if we have multiple replicas, do you shard the cache?
[22:10] Marcus: we have a consistent hashing layer for cache routing; cross-node replication for hot keys is optional.
[22:35] Tom: anything else on pilot instrumentation?
[22:45] Sofia: pilot will produce: cost delta report, hit-rate curves, quality regressions (if any), and a recommendation doc.
[23:05] Aisha: how long till we get a pilot estimate?
[23:15] Sofia: Marcus will run the bench and publish numbers in 3-5 days after we get your trace.
[23:35] Marcus: ok quick note on edge cases — if your prompts are heavily personalized (like merchant-specific instructions) prefix hit rate drops; in that case KV per-merchant caching can still help.
[24:00] Tom: what about encryption keys for KV in Dedicated vs Private?
[24:10] Marcus: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-kms); Private gives full control including HSM options. we'll send the KMS integration guide.
[24:40] Aisha: i'm also worried about cost spikes during cold start after a failover. any mitigations?
[24:55] Marcus: pre-warm strategies, gradual rollouts, and fallback to a higher-cost but lower-latency model are typical mitigations. we can configure automatic fallback policies.
[25:20] Sofia: quick pause — any blockers for you to start pilot?
[25:30] Aisha: we need legal to review pilot contract and security docs; infra needs sample traces.
[25:50] Sofia: noted, we'll send docs and sample contract.
[26:10] [short side conversation inaudible]
[27:00] Marcus: one more practical — when you sample traffic, try to include settlement spikes. that's where batching pays off.
[27:25] Aisha: ok noted.
[27:45] Tom: about monitoring — can we set alerts on miss-rate thresholds?
[27:55] Marcus: yes, you can define alerts per-route; we also emit metrics on cache evictions and avg rehydrate time.
[28:20] Lina: any recommended TTLs?
[28:30] Marcus: start with 1h-24h depending on how static prefixes are; the sheet has recommended defaults per use case.
[29:00] Sofia: closing section — recapping deliverables: Marcus runs bench after trace, Sofia sends deck+pricing+security, Lina shares trace and topology, legal reviews pilot.
[29:25] Aisha: timeline for bench?
[29:35] Marcus: 3-5 days.
[30:00] Tom: ok, final Q on cost accounting — do you provide token-level billing by route?
[30:10] Marcus: yes Console gives token-level cost by route, model, and time window; we also export CSVs for your finance team.
[30:35] Sofia: any last Qs?
[30:45] Aisha: none from me.
[31:00] Tom: i'm good.
[31:10] Lina: one more — do you support on-prem for certain models we want to keep local?
[31:25] Sofia: yes Private on-prem is supported; we'll talk more in deep dive.
[31:40] Marcus: ok that's the end of demo, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
[32:00] Sofia: thanks everyone, talk soon.
